1 STATISTICAL METHOD

Continuous variables are reported as median and interquartile range [IQR], whereas categorical variables are presented as counts and percentages. Baseline comparisons were performed by stratifying patients according to the median pre-implantation cDPP3 concentration into below median and above median cDPP3 groups. Considering the sample size and the exploratory, post hoc nature of this study, between-group differences are reported as Hodges–Lehmann estimates with 95% confidence intervals (derived from the Wilcoxon rank-sum test) for continuous variables, and as absolute differences in group proportions with 95% confidence intervals (estimated using the Agresti–Caffo method) for categorical variables. Continuous variables with a skewed distribution were log transformed for all subsequent models. Correlations between cDPP3 concentrations and continuous variables were evaluated using Spearman test. Variables measured at three predefined time points were compared using linear mixed-effects models with Kenward–Roger correction. Residuals of the models were checked. 30-day survival was evaluated in high and low cDPP3 groups drawing Kaplan–Meier curves. Heart transplantation and long-term mechanical circulatory support were treated as censoring events. A multivariable Cox model investigating the association between cDPP3 and the 30-day survival was performed: considering the sample size and the fact that cDPP3 is regarded as one of the main drivers highly correlated with clinico-biological severity and outcome, confounders were selected a priori and included cardiac arrest before VA-ECMO, cause of cardiogenic shock (ischemic or non-ischemic), the delay between ICU admission and VA-ECMO implantation. Model assumption was checked using Schoenfeld residuals. All statistical analyses were performed using R (version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31)). A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant and as the results were considered exploratory no adjustment for alpha multiplicity was performed.
